$comment: The demos list. One entry per game: the site pages, the home grid, sitemap, JSON-LD and `pnpm build:site` (which builds apps/<app> into play/<id>/) all read this file. Links without a scheme are relative to the site base. Every number in an entry must appear in apps/<app>/README.md, the game's committed README (node site/scripts/check-claims.mjs). See site/README.md. webglFallback: false when the demo does not render correctly on the WebGL fallback yet (the page then says so).

games.name: Ronin Outpost
games.blurb: Hold the gate against eight waves of the dead with a katana. Toon-shaded, with skinned zombie crowds.
games.pitch: A katana horde-defence game. You are a lone swordsman holding the community-hall gate through eight waves of the dead, from golden hour to dusk. Every cut is procedural sword technique on a real character skeleton, the undead shamble in on four different bodies, and the whole scene is cel-shaded with ink outlines over a Gaussian-splat capture of a real place.

controls.action: Light combo: three cuts, ending in the Crescent Sweep
Heavy attack; hold to charge Thunder Cleave
Dodge; dodge then Light for a dash-slash
Jump; Heavy in the air plunges
Spin Storm, when the Focus meter is full
Pick an upgrade after every second wave

features.title: Opt-in toon style
features.text: post.style: "toon" gives cel lighting, ink outlines from the depth and normal prepass, and a posterised grade on the splat. The default PBR path is unchanged.

features.title: Skinned crowds
features.text: Hordes of skinned zombies, 60-plus by wave 8, built from four Rocketbox civilians, with slowed walks, sprinting runners and larger brutes.

features.title: Procedural sword technique
features.text: Two-bone IK keeps both hands on the hilt, the torso twists into each swing, and the katana is parented to the hand bone.

features.title: A real place as the level
features.text: The arena is a Gaussian-splat capture of a community hall, composited with the meshes.

screenshots.alt: Ronin Outpost: the swordsman's Spin Storm whirls blade trails through a wave-5 crowd of zombies at the hall gate
Close-up of the masked swordsman in an indigo gi cutting in front of the hall gate
Wave 8: the swordsman spins through a horde of zombies in the yard

games.caption: Ronin Outpost · toon-shaded skinned crowds · runs in your browser

games.name: Swarm Siege
games.blurb: Top-down tower defence against a glowing tide of thousands of instanced enemies, simulated in a worker.
games.pitch: A top-down tower defence. Two rifts at the far corners of a night-time salt flat pour a glowing tide of creatures down ember-lit lanes that merge into one serpentine trunk ending at the Beacon. Place towers on the build pads beside the lanes, upgrade them, and hold for twelve waves. Wave 12 sends more than 7,000 enemies and peaks at about 6,000 alive at once.

controls.action: Choose a tower: Spark, Mortar, Frost or Lance
Place on the pad under the cursor, or select a tower
Begin, call the next wave early, or restart

features.title: Instancing at scale
features.text: Each enemy kind is one InstancedMesh; the Mite pool has 32,768 slots, with a per-instance glow read by a TSL emissive node.

features.title: A sim in a Web Worker
features.text: The whole game sim runs in a worker and posts packed snapshots; the main thread only renders.

links.label: Recipe: instanced crowds, workers and the fast build

features.title: Camera picking with raycasts
features.text: The cursor ray is an engine raycast that picks towers and build pads.

features.title: Seeded spawners for debris
features.text: A Brute's death drops debris shards from a runtime engine spawner as real rigid bodies.

screenshots.alt: Swarm Siege: a pink tide of creatures floods past glowing towers where the lanes merge
Top view of wave 12: thousands of creatures stream along the serpentine lane towards the Beacon
Lance beams and frost pulses cutting through the swarm

games.caption: Swarm Siege · thousands of instanced enemies from a worker

proof.label: live agents held at 60 fps in the best stress run

games.name: Breakpoint
games.blurb: Bring down towers built from 838 to 1,344 physics blocks, then watch your best shot re-simulated exactly.
games.pitch: Physics demolition. Fire heavy iron balls from a siege cannon at stone structures generated from a seed: a keep, a viaduct and a citadel, each built from 838 to 1,344 rigid bodies. You get three shots per site and score the mass you knock below the survey line. Then the game replays your best shot. The replay is not a recording: a second physics world rebuilds the site from its seed, is fed the same inputs, and checks its state hash against the live run on screen.

controls.action: Aim at a spot on a structure
Charge the shot, then release to fire
Replay your best shot, on the report card

features.title: Rapier at scale, off the main thread
features.text: 3,166 dynamic bodies over three sites on the SIMD fast build. The sim runs in a Web Worker and streams packed body states, so a heavy collapse slows game time instead of dropping frames.

links.label: Recipe: instanced crowds, workers and the fast build

features.title: Deterministic replay
features.text: Your best shot is stored as inputs and re-simulated from the seed, ending with a live state-hash check.

features.title: Shadows and AO on debris
features.text: Cascaded shadow maps, GTAO and bloom from the default pipeline, on one InstancedMesh per block kind.

features.title: Runtime spawns and impacts
features.text: Each shot spawns a ball body at runtime with a launch velocity; dust, chips and sound are driven from the physics state alone.

proof.label: dynamic bodies simulated in a Web Worker

games.name: Drift Drone
games.blurb: An FPV drone time trial through LED gates in a real 3D-scanned yard, against a re-simulated ghost.
games.tag: force-driven flight · splats · depth of field
games.pitch: An FPV drone time trial. Fly a racing quadcopter through LED gates around an old brick hall in a real Gaussian-splat capture: low over the garden beds, up past the windows and under the eaves. Your best lap comes back as a ghost, re-simulated from your own stick inputs, and the last crossing of the line is a slow-motion photo finish with depth of field. The drone is a plain dynamic body flown only by thrust and torque impulses.

controls.keys: Arrows or I J K L
controls.action: Tilt (assisted) or pitch and roll rates (acro)
Acro: ease the throttle back to hover
Left stick throttle and yaw, right stick pitch and roll

features.title: 6-DOF force-driven flight
features.text: A 0.8 kg dynamic sphere flown only by applyImpulse and applyTorqueImpulse, with a rate loop on angularVelocity.

features.title: Ghosts by re-simulation
features.text: Your best lap's input log is replayed in a second world in lockstep with you; tests check it is tick-for-tick identical.

features.title: Splat and mesh compositing at speed
features.text: Gates, the quad and its trails composite into the 800k-splat hall capture and cast shadows on the splat floor.

features.title: Photo-finish depth of field
features.text: The finish replay drives the renderer's depth of field onto the drone.

screenshots.alt: Drift Drone: the quadcopter climbs through a glowing yellow gate under the hall's eaves
FPV view flying past the brick hall's windows towards a pink gate

games.caption: Drift Drone · force-driven flight through a real capture

games.name: Ghostline
games.blurb: Marble time trials against a ghost that is re-simulated live from your inputs, not played back.
games.pitch: A marble time trial. Tilt the board and roll a glass, chrome or ember marble down three ribbon courses in the sky, with boosts, jumps, sweepers and checkpoints, against a translucent ghost of your best run. The ghost is never a recording: it is your run re-simulated by a second physics world fed the same seed and the same logged inputs, one tick at a time, in lockstep with you.

controls.action: Tilt the board (relative to the camera)
Retry and race your ghost again
Pick course and marble, ghost mode, race
Left stick tilts, A hops, B brakes

features.title: Ghosts from inputs
features.text: A run is fully defined by the course JSON, the seed and the input log. Inputs are quantised before logging, so the camera never leaks into the sim, and the results screen re-simulates your run headless to verify it.

features.title: Node and Chromium agree
features.text: The shipped par ghosts were recorded in Node and end on the same hash in the browser.

features.title: PBR marbles and courses
features.text: Iridescent clearcoat glass, mirror chrome and ember marbles on lacquered decks, with CSM shadows, GTAO and bloom.

features.title: JSON courses
features.text: Each course is an engine scene plus a turtle-style track that expands into trimesh colliders and meshes.

screenshots.alt: Ghostline: the glowing ember marble rolling down the Neon Undertow course

games.caption: Ghostline · ghosts re-simulated from your inputs

games.name: Skyrun
games.blurb: A parkour time trial across floating islands: ride ferries, lifts and a spinning wheel against your own ghost.
games.pitch: A third-person parkour time trial above a dawn cloud sea. Run, jump and ride across floating islands: climb stairs and ramps, hop onto shuttles, a ferry, lifts, a turnstile bridge, orbiting gondolas and a spinning wheel, collect sky shards, pass every checkpoint and reach the gold gate. Your best run comes back as a translucent ghost, re-simulated from your own inputs.

controls.action: Turn the camera (click to lock the mouse)

features.title: Riding moving platforms
features.text: The engine's opt-in character.ridePlatforms carries the runner exactly with sliding, spinning and orbiting kinematic platforms, and keeps their velocity as momentum on a jump.

features.title: The full character controller
features.text: accel, autostep up stairs, a slope limit, ground snap, coyote jump and teleport respawns, with a spring-arm camera.

features.title: Ghosts by re-simulation
features.text: Your best run is stored as its input log and replayed in a second world.

The runner riding a spinning wooden wheel platform
The runner at the glowing finish gate on Gale Spires

games.caption: Skyrun · a character riding kinematic platforms

games.name: Field Notes
games.blurb: Photograph luminous anomalies inside two real, 3D-captured places, with a working depth of field.
games.pitch: You are a field researcher with one roll of film. Six luminous, impossible objects have surfaced inside a real, photo-captured place. Walk the site in third person, follow the signal to find each one, then raise your camera and bring back a photograph worth keeping: composed on a third, filling the frame, in focus and correctly exposed. Twelve frames, five minutes of daylight, two survey sites.

controls.action: Release the shutter, with the camera up
Exposure down or up a third of a stop
Change survey site, on the title
Start, and a new survey from the results

features.title: Splat and mesh compositing
features.text: Two captures, an outdoor yard and an apartment courtyard. Meshes occlude splats and splats occlude meshes, with shadows on the splat floor through the engine's shadow catcher.

features.title: Opt-in depth of field
features.text: Photo mode blurs the splat and the meshes together, with focus, zoom and exposure through the tone mapper.

features.title: Kinematic character controller
features.text: The researcher is the engine's Rust character controller with a third-person spring-arm camera.

features.title: Raycast scoring
features.text: Each photo's occlusion penalty is an engine raycast from the lens to the subject.

screenshots.alt: Field Notes: photo mode with eye-autofocus on a chrome knot floating in a real scanned yard
The researcher walking through the scanned apartment towards a glowing anomaly, with a developed print
A scanned wicker chair and glass wall drawn in front of a glowing mesh door

games.caption: Field Notes · meshes composited into real splat captures

games.name: Ringout
games.blurb: Local multiplayer sumo for up to four on a collapsing, spinning arena, with a replay that proves itself.
games.pitch: A local multiplayer sumo arena. Up to four heavy orbs roll on a spinning arena of 61 hexagonal basalt columns. Shove, dash and knock the others off the edge while the arena collapses ring by ring from the outside in. Two people share one keyboard and bots fill the other seats. After every round, an instant replay re-simulates the round from its input log and shows on screen that it reproduces the live state hash.

controls.action: Change the seats and the match length

features.title: Impulses and torque
features.text: Orbs are dynamic spheres driven by torque impulses about the rolling axis plus small steering impulses. A dash is one big impulse with a cooldown.

features.title: Kinematic movers
features.text: Every column is a kinematic body posed each tick with setKinematicPose: the arena turns, warned rings shake, and tiles drop in a seeded order.

features.title: Instant replay with a hash proof
features.text: The replay rebuilds the round in a fresh world from its seed and input log and compares state hashes on screen.

screenshots.alt: Ringout: the outer ring of hex columns glows and drops while three orbs clash in the middle
Two glowing orbs meet at the start of a round on the hex arena
The instant replay, with the re-simulated state hash matching the live round

games.caption: Ringout · impulses, kinematic movers and a verified replay

games.name: Rockfall
games.blurb: Dodge escalating waves of falling rocks, with up to 1,800 live rigid bodies in the pit.
games.pitch: An arcade survival game. The walls of a desert quarry are coming down: rocks, slate slabs, boulders and finally molten meteors rain into a walled pit in escalating waves. Read the impact markers, dodge, push through the rubble, grab crystals, and stay standing as long as you can. Every falling rock comes from an engine spawner: the game never places a rock itself.

controls.action: Move; the camera never turns, so W is always up
Jump over rubble or a rolling boulder
Start a run, or restart from the results

features.title: Rust-side seeded spawners
features.text: The wave director only creates spawner entities: a template body, a rate, a count, an area and a seed. The engine decides when and where each rock appears.

features.title: Thousands of live bodies
features.text: Up to 1,400 convex-hull bodies on the deterministic build and 1,800 on the fast build, drawn as one InstancedMesh per rock kind.

features.title: A character that pushes bodies
features.text: The player is the kinematic character controller; it shoves pebbles aside while boulders barely move.

features.title: Raycast impact markers
features.text: Each landing point is predicted ballistically, and an engine raycast finds the top of the rubble under it.

games.caption: Rockfall · engine spawners and up to 1,800 live bodies

games.name: Lanternfall
games.blurb: A stealth heist in a keep generated fresh from a seed every run. Stay out of the lantern light.
games.pitch: A stealth heist in a keep that is generated fresh from a seed every run. You are a thief in a moonlit stone keep guarded by brass automaton wardens. Steal the Ember Relic from the hall farthest from the gate, take what gold you pass, and walk back out. Lantern light shows you to the guards: in the dark they see you only from a step or two away, in a lantern pool from across the room. Every keep is a real Pebble3D scene, written by a seeded generator and checked by the schema.

controls.action: Run; guards within 7 m hear it and come to look
Begin, or retry the same keep after a result

features.title: Runtime scene generation
features.text: A seed becomes a schema-valid scene JSON with rooms, doorways, cover, lanterns and guards, then loads through createGame. Tests flood-fill every seed from 1 to 10,000 to prove the relic, the exit and every room are reachable.

links.label: Recipe: JSON levels and headless verify

features.title: Raycast perception
features.text: Each guard's sight is a static-only engine raycast from its eye to the thief, with a reach that scales with the light on the thief's tile. Walls and pillars are real cover.

features.title: Characters with accel
features.text: The thief and the guards are engine characters: kinematic capsules with eased acceleration, driven only by input intents.

features.title: Deterministic runs
features.text: Fixed 60 Hz ticks and a seeded generator: the Node test reproduces the browser capture exactly.

games.name: Chain Reaction
games.blurb: Contraption puzzles whose levels are JSON and whose solutions are verified headless in Node.
games.pitch: A contraption puzzle on a studio pegboard. Each level gives you a few parts: ramps, dominoes, springs, fans and see-saws. Place them on the grid, press Run, and watch the chain play out. Get the red ball into the glowing cup using as few parts as possible. Every run is a deterministic engine simulation, so the same parts always produce the same run, down to the last bit of the state hash.

controls.action: Choose a part from the tray
Place a part on a cell
Run the machine; again to reset

features.title: Levels are JSON
features.text: Each level is puzzle data plus a partial engine scene, merged over a base scene and parsed by the SDK's schema like any other scene.

links.label: Recipe: JSON levels and headless verify

features.title: A headless verifier
features.text: pnpm --filter chain-reaction verify runs every reference solution in Node on the same wasm and checks the goal, par and the stored state hash.

features.title: Browser and Node agree
features.text: The result card shows when your run's hash matches the one the Node verifier stored.

features.title: Impulses as gameplay
features.text: Springs and fans apply impulses before each tick through World.applyImpulse.

games.caption: Chain Reaction · solutions verified headless in Node

games.name: Pebble Garden
games.blurb: A physics sandbox and level editor whose gardens export as scene JSON and import with readable errors.
games.tag: scene JSON · validation · play and rewind
games.pitch: A physics sandbox and level editor. Place pieces on a sand garden with the mouse, move, rotate and scale them with a gizmo, set their colour and body type, then press Play to simulate and press it again to rewind exactly. Every garden is a Pebble3D scene: Export writes schema-valid scene JSON, and Import opens any scene JSON with readable error messages. A human can build what an agent writes, and the reverse.

controls.action: Pick one of the ten palette pieces

features.title: Scenes as a product feature
features.text: Export writes tidy, schema-valid scene JSON; tests check each starter garden survives export and import with the same state hash.

features.title: Readable validation
features.text: Import reports a syntax error's line and column, and every schema problem with its field path, line and a suggestion for a misspelt key.

features.title: Play and rewind
features.text: Play runs on the deterministic build, so two plays from the same edit give the same hash.

features.title: Kinematic motors
features.text: Kinematic pieces turn about their own up axis on Play, driven by setKinematicPose.
